<PAGE><|det|>header [114, 95, 395, 125]<|/det|>5. Bug Reports
<|det|>text [114, 185, 378, 207]<|/det|>Bug ID #1[ Acknowledged ]
<|det|>title [113, 241, 592, 262]<|/det|>Missing zero _minOut validation while swapping
<|det|>title [113, 302, 260, 319]<|/det|>Vulnerability Type
<|det|>text [114, 321, 302, 337]<|/det|>Missing Input Validation
<|det|>title [113, 360, 185, 377]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [114, 380, 154, 396]<|/det|>High
<|det|>title [113, 418, 210, 435]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [112, 437, 884, 531]<|/det|>The claimCompAndConvertTo() function allows swapping COMP tokens to a specified token using a DEX router. The function accepts a __minOut parameter that determines the minimum output amount when performing the swap. However, the function does not validate that this value is greater than zero. When a keeper or governor calls this function with __minOut set to 0, they effectively approve any amount of tokens in return, even if it's substantially below market value.
<|det|>title [114, 552, 231, 567]<|/det|>Affected Code
<|det|>text [142, 571, 880, 607]<|/det|>- https://github.com/hemilabs/vusd-stablecoin/blob/54f9f235f26df813152b3d3235e7f4373c e473b6/contracts/Treasury.sol#.L168-L187
<|det|>title [113, 629, 185, 644]<|/det|>Impacts
<|det|>text [112, 647, 885, 740]<|/det|>A malicious keeper can exploit this by front-running the transaction and manipulating the pool's price, causing the function to receive far fewer tokens than what would be fair for the input amount. This can lead to direct fund loss for the protocol as the swap could execute at highly unfavorable rates. MEV bots can also target these transactions, further extracting value from the protocol.
<|det|>title [113, 763, 219, 777]<|/det|>Remediation
<|det|>text [113, 782, 678, 798]<|/det|>It is recommended to add a validation to the _minOut is not equal to zero.
<|det|>title [113, 821, 174, 835]<|/det|>Retest
<|det|>text [113, 839, 655, 856]<|/det|>Client's comment: Won't fix assuming the keeper role is a trusted role.
